findings.description: [expert] Using `daemon=False` for the background execution thread causes the CLI process to block indefinitely on exit, as Python's `sys.exit()` joins all non-daemon threads. This completely defeats the architectural intent of an "async" measurement and will cause `code-forge review --mode ci` to hang for ~10+ minutes. Furthermore, since threads share the process PID, tracking `os.getpid()` is flawed for detecting whether this background task is still alive across runs, because the PID tracked is just the CLI's PID. You should spawn a completely detached background OS process (e.g., using `subprocess.Popen` with `start_new_session=True` or a double-fork daemonization) rather than trying to outlive the main process with a thread.

[expert] The test explicitly enforces `daemon is False` to ensure the mutation completes, which enforces the bug causing the CLI to hang. When the mutation logic is refactored to spawn a separate OS process, this test will need to be rewritten to assert process detachment constraints (e.g. `start_new_session=True`) rather than thread configuration.

from .factories import (
    build_autofixer,
    build_falsifier,
    build_l1_provider,
    build_l2_runner,
    build_revert_fn,
)

# Without this the state machine falls back to its no-op
            # default, whose ([], []) is byte-identical to a mutation run
            # that found no survivors -- the CLI reported a gate it never
            # ran. build_l2_runner degrades to MUTATION_SKIPPED when mutmut
            # is absent, so this costs nothing where it cannot measure.
            l2_runner=build_l2_runner(),

# Both sibling skips below say why they skipped. Without
                # this one the gate simply never launches: no finding, no
                # error, and a PASS indistinguishable from a run where
                # mutation actually measured something. A worktree carries
                # its own gitignored gate.yaml, so an incomplete one is the
                # common case rather than a rare misconfiguration.
                self._state.infra_errors.append(
                    "CI: mutation skipped -- gate.yaml missing or "
                    "test.command not configured: %s" % exc
                )

# Not a daemon: the interpreter joins non-daemon threads at
                # exit. As a daemon it was killed the instant the review
                # process returned, so it never wrote past its own "running"
                # marker, and every later round read a dead PID and dismissed
                # the gate instead of measuring anything. run_mutation bounds
                # itself (120s baseline + 600s mutmut + 10s results).
                thread = threading.Thread(
                    target=_async_mutation, daemon=False
                )

assert "l2_runner" in captured, (
            "the CLI built its StateMachine without l2_runner. The machine "
            "then falls back to a no-op default returning ([], []), which "
            "reads exactly like a mutation run that found no survivors."
        )
        assert captured["l2_runner"] is not _DEFAULT_L2, (
            "l2_runner was passed, but it is the machine's own no-op "
            "default rather than a runner that can measure anything."
        )

assert captured["daemon"] is False, (
            "mutation thread was launched with daemon=%r. A daemon thread is "
            "killed when the review process exits, so the run dies before "
            "writing its result and the gate silently degrades to SKIPPED."
            % captured["daemon"]
        )

assert any(
            "test.command not configured" in e
            for e in sm._state.infra_errors
        ), (
            "mutation was skipped for an unusable gate.yaml and left no "
            "trace: infra_errors=%r. The verdict then reads identically to "
            "one where the mutation gate actually ran."
            % sm._state.infra_errors
        )
